sources.entry: Atheos - Web-based IDE framework with a small footprint and minimal requirements, continued from Codiad. (Source Code) MIT PHP/Docker

summary.one_liner: Atheos is a web-based IDE framework, a maintained fork of Codiad, meant to be small, fast, and easy to run on a server.
summary.what_it_does: Atheos is a browser-based code editor and IDE that runs on a PHP/JavaScript web server rather than on the desktop. The README says it was rewritten from Codiad to use more modern tooling and includes a more complete user permission system. It has built-in Git integration and uses POST requests to the server instead of GET. The project aims to reduce server-to-client traffic and removes jQuery. It is designed around standardized components so plugins and themes can be added, and it includes a built-in update check that notifies the admin of new versions.
use_cases: Edit code in a browser on a self-hosted server
Run a cloud-based IDE without a large server footprint
Develop code with built-in Git integration
Manage per-user access to an online code workspace
Build plugins or themes for a web IDE
how_to_run: Place the Atheos files in a web-accessible folder on a PHP-capable web server
Make /config.php, /data, /workspace, /plugins and /themes writable by the web server
Open the folder in a browser and follow the installation screen
Alternatively, install using the Docker image on DockerHub (command not given in README)
notable: Maintained fork of Codiad, substantially rewritten
Standardized component structure to encourage plugins
caveats: Primarily developed and tested on a Debian LAMP stack; other stacks may have issues
No built-in self-update; admins must copy files manually when upgrading
Update system is described as currently being rewritten
